_note: Which documents prove which activities. The 'facts' block drives the deterministic evidence check; the chunks are the citable prose. Simplified for demonstration.

chunks.title: Proving work hours
chunks.text: Pay stubs covering the month are the cleanest proof of employment hours. If pay stubs are unavailable — cash pay, a small employer, lost records — an employer letter stating hours works, and where records genuinely cannot be produced, a self-attestation with the employer's contact information is accepted while the state verifies. Cash work counts; undocumented does not mean unprovable.

chunks.title: Proving self-employment
chunks.text: Self-employment is proven with an income ledger, tax records, or client invoices. Hours may be computed from income at a reasonable rate when direct hour records are not kept. Keep a simple weekly log going forward — it becomes the easiest renewal you will ever do.

chunks.title: Proving school and training
chunks.text: An enrollment letter or class schedule proves education hours; half-time enrollment or more satisfies the standard by itself in most months. Job-training and workforce programs are proven with a program enrollment letter or attendance log — the program office produces these routinely on request.

chunks.title: Proving community service
chunks.text: Community service is proven with a volunteer log signed by the organization or a letter from it stating dates and hours. Ask the organization for the letter before the renewal month ends — a two-line letter is enough.

chunks.title: Keep copies of everything
chunks.text: Keep a copy, photo, or confirmation number for every document you submit and every report you make. If the state's record and yours ever disagree, your copy with a date is what restores coverage quickly.
